inputs.original_text: M.K. Stalin’s DMK manifesto is heavy on handouts: doubling women’s monthly aid to Rs 2,000, Rs 8,000 household coupons, and free motor pumpsets for farmers. These may be presented as help, but voters should ask how such promises will be paid for and whether they strengthen families and self-reliance—or make more people dependent on government. FDI, jobs and AI development sound more forward-looking, while support for fishermen matters too; still, a serious plan should put lasting work and economic responsibility ahead of ever-expanding giveaways.
inputs.modified_text: M.K. Stalin’s DMK is making government handouts the centerpiece: doubling women’s monthly aid to Rs 2,000, Rs 8,000 household coupons and free motor pumpsets for farmers. These promises may win applause, but they risk making families more reliant on the state instead of strengthening self-reliance and responsibility. FDI, jobs and AI development point toward a more durable path, and support for fishermen matters—but lasting work and sound economic priorities should come before an ever-growing list of giveaways.
